summary: This is a React component that scaffolds project file structures. It accepts either individual file snippets as children or a flat object of files, then provides three ways for users to set up the project: viewing files with syntax highlighting, generating a bash script to recreate the folder structure, or downloading everything as a ZIP archive. It also supports empty folders and post-install guidelines.

explanations.22: Object.assign() here attaches a marker property (isGuideline: true) to a dummy component so we can identify Guideline elements later when processing children, even if they're wrapped by other components.
explanations.28: Similar to Guideline, this creates a marker component to identify empty folders that should be created but don't contain files.
explanations.49: Children.forEach is React's utility to safely iterate over the children prop, which can be a single element, an array, or nested structure.
explanations.52: If a child is a React element (like a wrapper), we recursively extract its nested text content to handle MDX-wrapped content like paragraphs inside guidelines.
explanations.86: We store a reference to the setTimeout ID so we can clean it up later and prevent memory leaks when the component unmounts.
explanations.95: useMemo caches the parsed file list, guidelines, and folders so they're only recalculated when the input data (files or children) changes, not on every render.
explanations.113: We type-cast child.type to check for our marker properties (isGuideline, isEmptyFolder) since the type system doesn't know about these custom properties we attached.
explanations.130: This checks if the child is a Snippet component, has a filename prop, or has both a title and is a custom component (not an HTML element like div)—these patterns indicate it's a file to include.
explanations.141: We check for content in two places: the code prop (injected by a remark plugin) or as direct string children, with code taking priority because it's the actual file content, not just a path.
explanations.155: useMemo prevents the bash script from being regenerated whenever UI state (like copied status) changes, since it only depends on the file data.
explanations.167: We use a heredoc with a custom delimiter to safely embed file content in bash, including content with special characters or newlines, and mkdir -p ensures parent directories exist.
explanations.173:
getGuidelineText extracts plain text from guidelines (stripping MDX wrappers like

tags), then normalizes whitespace so the bash echo command displays nicely.
explanations.204: We strip leading slashes from the folder name because some paths like '/tmp/...' would create invalid or unsafe zip archive paths.
explanations.209: JSZip.folder() returns null only on invalid folder names, but since we've sanitized safeFolderName, we throw an error if it still somehow fails so users see a clear message.
explanations.227: generateAsync({ type: 'blob' }) creates the binary zip file in memory; we then convert it to a downloadable object URL that browsers can trigger through a fake link.
explanations.233: We append the link to the DOM before clicking because Firefox requires the element to be in the document, whereas Chrome doesn't—this ensures cross-browser compatibility.
explanations.341: We use React.cloneElement to preserve the original Snippet component with its styling and behavior, just updating the content and defaultOpen props based on expandAll state.
